title: Replace overstimulating screen time with Montessori-inspired Pok Pok for just $60
content:
Macworld

TL;DR: Pok Pok lifetime access is $59.99 (reg. $250), giving families unlimited access to a growing collection of low-stimulation, Montessori-inspired educational activities without ads, levels, winning, or losing.

Not all kids’ screen time needs flashing rewards, competitive levels, or an ad appearing every 30 seconds. Pok Pok takes a calmer route, and lifetime access is currently $59.99 instead of $250.

Designed for kids ages 2–8, Pok Pok is a Montessori-inspired digital playroom built around exploration rather than winning. No rules, levels, objectives, or losing. Kids simply choose a toy and start experimenting.

The activities sneak plenty of learning into that play. Pok Pok supports foundational skills involving STEM, numbers, language, problem-solving, cause and effect, and cognitive, social, and emotional development.

Kids can explore outer space, count their way through Number Journey, experiment with Shapes, dress characters, meet dinosaurs, solve World Puzzles, visit Islands, and more.

Pok Pok is also intentionally low-stimulation. Its art is hand-drawn, while sound effects and music are recorded in-house to create a gentler environment. There are no attempts to trick kids into making purchases.

It works offline, which could make it particularly handy for travel, and one account provides family access across all your family’s devices. New toys, plus seasonal and cultural updates, are also added regularly.

Get lifetime Pok Pok access for just $59.99 (reg. $250) right now.
